clue.text: Biscuits not all there ?

definitions.meaning: thin crisp savoury biscuits eaten with cheese

explanation.surface: A packet of biscuits that seems to have some missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackers are dry biscuits, and in British slang someone crackers is mad, mentally lacking.

clue.text: Bird finds girl in at break

indicators.note: to break the words is to smash their letters and rebuild them

explanation.surface: A man finds his girlfriend at work during a tea break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' rearranges GIRL and IN AT. A ringtail is the female hen harrier, named for its banded tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringtail is a female or young hen harrier, a bird of prey with a barred tail.

clue.text: Stars as king and rustic lover

parts.note: Charles is the name of English kings
a swain is a country youth or lover in pastoral poetry

explanation.surface: Celebrities cast as a monarch and his country sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' and 'and' are links. Charles's Wain is the old British name for the Plough, the Big Dipper.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles's Wain is the Plough, the seven bright stars of the Great Bear constellation.

clue.text: Sign given in garden about six, before church

indicators.note: the garden part comes before the church in the answer
the garden goes round the six

parts.note: Eden is the garden of Genesis
VI is six in Roman numerals
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A notice put up in a garden for half a dozen people heading to church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign given in' tempts a reading of the definition as a placard; 'about' is the container signal around the Roman six.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidence is an indication or token that something is so, a sign of it.

clue.text: Sea-side hairdo

definitions.meaning: a short layered women's haircut of the 1920s

explanation.surface: A holiday hairstyle for the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses share one word: beach pebbles and a 1920s bob tapering at the nape.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingle is beach gravel, and also a cropped hairstyle tapered at the back of the neck.

clue.text: Dracula in the army?

parts.note: the vampire turns into a bat, so he is a ..., and in the forces that is an officer's servant

explanation.surface: The vampire count enlists as a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: In the British army a batman is an officer's personal servant; Dracula, who becomes a bat, is also a bat-man.
explanation.definitionFit: A batman is a soldier acting as an officer's orderly, and Dracula is a man who becomes a bat.

clue.text: Pierce ends when raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read from the bottom up

parts.note: tips are ends or points

explanation.surface: A needle's points jab when they are lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when raised' turns TIPS upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To spit is to impale on a skewer, as meat is pierced for roasting.

clue.text: Theatre man carries tin opener for caviare container, perhaps

indicators.note: the theatre man holds the opened letter inside him

parts.note: a surgeon works in an operating theatre

indicators.note: an opener is what starts something, so the word tin gives its first letter

explanation.surface: An actor brings a can opener to open a jar of fish eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' is the operating theatre, not the stage. 'opener' takes T from 'tin', which 'carries' puts inside SURGEON.
explanation.definitionFit: The sturgeon is the fish whose roe is caviare, so it literally holds the delicacy.

clue.text: So the tap needs changing? A sensitive point:

indicators.note: the letters of the three words are to be changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A plumber notes that a faucet must be replaced, a touchy subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs changing' rearranges the eight letters of SO THE TAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A heat-spot is a point on the skin that senses warmth, one of its sensitive points.

clue.text: One seen in and about Peru .

definitions.text: One seen in and about Peru

parts.note: taken as written
CA is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A traveller spotted in and around Peru.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a member of the old Peruvian empire while also giving IN plus CA (circa).
explanation.definitionFit: The Incas were the native people ruling the Andean empire centred on Peru.

clue.text: Would he note some falling off in new pupils?

definitions.text: Would he note some falling off in new pupils?

parts.words: Would he note some falling off in new pupils
parts.note: the pupils are learner horsemen and the falling off is tumbling from the saddle, not a drop in numbers

explanation.surface: A teacher wonders whether attendance is declining among fresh students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling off' reads as a decline, but here novices literally fall off their horses, watched by their instructor.
explanation.definitionFit: A riding-master teaches equestrian skills, so beginners tumbling from horses is his daily sight.

clue.text: American writer joins stage female weight-lifter

parts.note: a step is a stage in a process
a hen is a female bird
a crane is a machine that lifts heavy weights

explanation.surface: A US author takes to the boards with a strongwoman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joins' is a link. Stephen Crane wrote The Red Badge of Courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Crane was a nineteenth-century novelist from New Jersey, author of The Red Badge of Courage.

clue.text: Prohibition about fish being returned in part of Moby Dick

indicators.note: the ban word goes round the fish

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition

indicators.note: returned means the fish word is turned backwards here

parts.note: an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A ban surrounds some fish thrown back during a chapter of the whaling novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being returned' turns the fish backwards before 'about' wraps the ban round it. Moby Dick is the whale in Herman Melville's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Baleen is whalebone, the filtering plates in a great whale's mouth such as the white whale's.

clue.text: Fish the lake in your underwear?

parts.note: ling is a food fish of the cod family
Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a fish and lake water inside their undergarments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link: LING then ERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's undergarments, intimate apparel.

clue.text: Cuts a flogging after direction

indicators.note: the flogging comes after the direction in the answer

parts.note: S is south, a compass direction
lashes are strokes of the whip, a flogging

explanation.surface: A disciplinary report: strokes of the whip ordered by a superior.
explanation.definitionFit: Slashes are long cuts, gashes made with a blade.

clue.text: Cocktails for TT passengers?

definitions.meaning: a brandy, orange liqueur and lemon mixed drink
the Isle of Man TT motorcycle races, where a passenger rides beside the bike

explanation.surface: Teetotal travellers are offered mixed drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: TT reads as teetotal, odd beside cocktails, but it is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man, which has sidecar classes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is a brandy-based mixed drink, and also the attached passenger car of a motorbike.

clue.text: Possibly his love is shown in cooler style

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are displayed inside the cooler

parts.note: a fan cools you

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged another way

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A romantic partner turns up displayed in a refrigerated cabinet with flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' scrambles the letters of 'his' with love's zero, and 'is shown in' sets the result inside the cooling device.
explanation.definitionFit: Fashion means the current mode or manner of dress, a prevailing style.

clue.text: Woolly-minded old sailor ?

parts.note: the ancient Greek mariner whose mind was set on a fleece, not a muddled thinker

explanation.surface: A confused elderly seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woolly-minded' suggests vague, but it means intent on wool: Jason's crew sailed the Argo to seize the Golden Fleece.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argonauts were Jason's crew aboard the Argo seeking the Golden Fleece.

clue.text: First move towards negotiations being conducted

definitions.meaning: an opening approach or proposal in talks
an orchestral prelude performed under a conductor

explanation.surface: Talks between parties are under way after an opening approach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conducted' reads as negotiations being carried on, but it is a piece of music led by a conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: An overture is an opening proposal, and also an orchestral introduction played under a baton.

clue.text: Harsh note given to sailor

parts.note: G is a musical note
a rating is a sailor without officer rank

explanation.surface: A stern message handed to a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given to' is a link. In the Royal Navy a rating is an ordinary sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A grating sound is rasping and rough, unpleasant to hear.

clue.text: Bird performed a piano duet before the queen

indicators.note: the earlier pieces come before the queen in the answer

parts.note: did is a past tense of do, performed

indicators.note: a duet is two performers, so the piano letter appears twice

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the queen

explanation.surface: A concert: two pianists played together in front of Her Majesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duet' doubles P to give PP. A didapper is the little grebe, a diving bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A didapper is an old name for the dabchick or little grebe, a small diving waterbird.

clue.text: No help dispensing acid

indicators.note: a chemist dispensing mixes things up, so the letters are made up anew

explanation.surface: A pharmacist refuses assistance while handing out a corrosive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispensing' rearranges NO HELP.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenol, carbolic acid, is a mildly acidic compound used as a disinfectant.

clue.text: Flower sacred to-Hindus.

parts.note: a flower here is a thing that flows, a river, and the one Hindus revere is in India

explanation.surface: A blossom held holy in Hindu worship, like the lotus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' suggests a bloom such as the lotus, but it is a thing that flows, a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ganges is India's holy river, where Hindus bathe and scatter ashes.

clue.text: Parry has roughly the right tone of voice

parts.note: to counter a blow is to parry it

indicators.note: roughly says the letters are put together in a loose, rearranged way

explanation.surface: A fencer's defensive move is delivered in a coarse manner of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' scrambles right's abbreviation with 'tone' to make the singing voice that follows the parry; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A countertenor is the highest adult male singing voice, above tenor, near alto.

clue.text: Some fanciful name for a bone?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone invents a whimsical title for a skeleton part.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'for a bone' included the link word 'for', which cannot stand in for a noun; the definition is 'a bone'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is the inner long forearm bone, on the little-finger side.

clue.text: River in which we keep chickens

definitions.meaning: a river in Sussex, southern England
a run is an enclosure where poultry are kept, read as a run

explanation.surface: Someone describes the stream where they rear their hens.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as A RUN, a chicken enclosure. The Arun is a river in the English county of West Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arun is an English waterway, and a hen run is a fenced poultry pen.

clue.text: Disparages scores' made by 'county

parts.note: runs are what a batsman scores in cricket
Down is a county of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Cricket talk: the runs totalled by a county side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made by' is a link. Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: To run down someone is to belittle or criticise them, an idiom for disparaging.

clue.text: Was as drippy as a yellow press editor?

parts.note: the gutter press is sensationalist journalism, also called the yellow press

explanation.surface: Asking whether a sensationalist tabloid's boss is wet and feeble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drippy' suggests a feeble person, but a candle that guttered dripped wax as it flickered.
explanation.definitionFit: A candle guttered when its wax ran down in drips as the flame wavered.
